chemicals.concentration_notes: ◦ High Potency: Ingestion of even a small amount of the fruit (fresh or dried) can be sufficient to cause kidney failure. ◦ Variable Sensitivity: There is individual variation; some cats may ingest these fruits without apparent ill effects, while others develop severe acute kidney failure. ◦ Concentrated Sources: Dried forms like raisins and currants (Zante currants) are particularly dangerous.
chemicals.description: ◦ Nephrotoxicity (Kidney Damage): These compounds are considered the primary toxic principles responsible for causing acute kidney failure in cats and dogs. ◦ Rapid Onset: The toxins are rapidly absorbed, often leading to vomiting within 12 hours, followed by diarrhea, lethargy, and increased thirst as kidney function declines.
chemicals.name: Tartaric Acid and its salt, Potassium Bitartrate (Cream of Tartar)

description:
Grapes, raisins, sultanas, and currants are highly dangerous for cats. There is no known safe amount. Even one grape or a few raisins may be enough to cause a serious problem in some cats.

The exact toxin is still not fully confirmed, though tartaric acid is one leading suspect. The main danger is sudden kidney injury. Because cats react unpredictably, a small amount can be risky even if another cat once seemed fine after eating more.

Early signs may include vomiting, diarrhea, low energy, not eating, belly pain, or increased thirst. Kidney problems can develop later. If your cat eats any grape, raisin, sultana, or currant, contact a veterinarian or pet poison helpline immediately instead of waiting for symptoms.
emergencyNote: Induction of Emesis (Vomiting) and Administration of Activated Charcoal
name: Grapes / Raisins / Currants
safetyNotes: Main hazard: Vitis fruits can cause unpredictable kidney injury; no safe amount is known.
Higher-risk forms: Raisins, sultanas, and dried currants are concentrated, so small amounts matter.
Symptoms: Vomiting, diarrhea, belly pain, low energy, poor appetite, increased thirst, or reduced urination.
Action: Call a vet or poison helpline immediately after any grape, raisin, sultana, or currant ingestion.

symptoms.name: Vomiting, diarrhea, belly pain, or low energy
symptoms.onset: Often within the first several hours after ingestion.

symptoms.name: Poor appetite, weakness, or worsening sickness
symptoms.onset: May develop as kidney injury begins.

symptoms.name: Increased thirst, reduced urination, or acute kidney failure
symptoms.onset: May develop over the next 24 to 72 hours.

treatments.description: If the ingestion was recent, the veterinarian will administer prescription medication to induce vomiting, removing the fruit from the stomach before the toxins are fully absorbed45. This is typically followed by the administration of activated charcoal (often with a cathartic) to bind any remaining toxins in the gastrointestinal tract and prevent them from entering the bloodstream.
treatments.name: Induction of Emesis (Vomiting) and Administration of Activated Charcoal
treatments.notes: Owners should not attempt to induce vomiting at home using salt or hydrogen peroxide, as this is unsafe for cats and can cause severe injury or poisoning4. This procedure is most effective when performed within hours of ingestion.

treatments.description: The veterinarian will administer IV fluids to correct dehydration and, crucially, to support the kidneys. Fluid therapy helps to "flush" the kidneys (diuresis), maintaining urine production and helping to clear toxins from the body.
treatments.name: Intravenous (IV) Fluid Diuresis
treatments.notes: Because grapes and raisins target the kidneys, fluid therapy is essential to prevent the onset of anuria (the cessation of urine production), which is a fatal complication of acute renal failure1011. Treatment may need to continue for 48 to 72 hours to ensure the kidneys are protected.

treatments.description: The veterinary team will run blood tests to establish baseline levels for kidney function, specifically checking creatinine, BUN (blood urea nitrogen), and electrolyte levels5. These tests are repeated (often every 24 hours) to track the progression of the toxicity or the success of the treatment.
treatments.name: Renal Function Monitoring (Biochemistry Profile)
treatments.notes: Clinical signs of kidney failure from grapes may not appear immediately; vomiting often starts within 12 hours, but severe renal failure markers may take 24 hours to days to manifest512. Therefore, monitoring is critical even if the cat appears fine initially.
